request.spec: Reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner. Respond with 409.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner. Respond with 409.

agent.result_text:
All 260 tests pass, including the new `Cp03Tests` and the previously-passing `Cp01Tests`/`Cp02Tests`.

## What I changed

**The rule** — `RejectDuplicateOwner.java`: broadened the duplicate check to reject an owner whose telephone matches **any** existing owner (previously it required matching last name *and* telephone). It scans `ownerRepository.findAll()` and throws `DuplicateOwnerException` → 409 on a telephone collision. This runs after `build` and before `save`, so the new owner isn't yet persisted when the check runs.

The `owners.POST.yml` pipeline already had the `rejectDuplicate` step wired in, and `DuplicateOwnerExceptionHandler` already maps the exception to 409, so no wiring changes were needed.

**Two pre-existing tests** — `OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.createOwnerSuccess` and `createDuplicateOwnerReturnsConflict` posted new owners using telephone `6085551023`, which is the seed owner George Franklin's number. Under the old (last-name + telephone) rule they didn't collide because the last names differed, but the new telephone-only rule correctly rejects them. Since the spec mandates that behavior, I updated those two tests to use non-seed telephones (`7085551023` / `7085552023`) so they exercise successful creation as intended. The duplicate-conflict test still validates 409 by posting the same body twice.

The cp02 rule remains satisfied (a same-telephone case is a strict subset of what the broader rule rejects), and cp02's "same last name, different telephone is allowed" case still passes.
